answer: Every agent mints its identity inside a secure enclave and anchors the key to a hardware attestation quote renewed each epoch. A quote cannot be forged, so one physical chip can only echo one registered identity; a thousand cloned keys would need a thousand real processors, each bought, powered, and renewed on schedule. Verifiers treat stale or repeated quotes as a comet trail - bright, fast, and gone - and refuse payout to any forge of duplicate identities.
